html:
Trinidad is the southernmost island of the Caribbean, just off the coast of Venezuela, and the larger half of the state of Trinidad and Tobago.

Columbus sighted it in 1498 and named it for the Holy Trinity. Spain founded a town in 1592 but the colony stayed thinly settled for two centuries. In 1783 Spain opened it to Catholic settlers, and French planters arrived with enslaved Africans to grow sugar and cocoa.

Britain captured the island in 1797. After the end of slavery in the 1830s, planters brought indentured workers from India, whose descendants now make up a large part of the population. Tobago was joined to Trinidad in 1889. Oil was found in the early 1900s and became the backbone of the economy.

Under Eric Williams, Trinidad and Tobago became independent in 1962 and a republic in 1976. The island gave the world calypso and the steelpan, the steel drum.
sum: Trinidad is the southernmost island of the Caribbean, just off the coast of Venezuela, and the larger half of the state of Trinidad and Tobago.
